products.name: TESmart HKS801-P23 8-Port HDMI KVM Switch, 4K 60 Hz, USB 3.0, RS232/LAN Control
specs: Front buttons, keyboard hotkeys, IR remote, RS232; LAN control in TESmart's listing title
products.warranty: 1-year limited warranty in the US. Registering the KVM with TESmart extends it (TESmart's support pages say 2 to 3 years).
products.returns: 30-day returns on tesmart.com; free US shipping.
products.summary: An 8-PC KVM for one 4K 60 Hz HDMI monitor, with USB 3.0 sharing, an EDID emulator on every port and RS232/LAN control.
products.fit: A desk, bench or small rack with up to 8 computers on one 4K screen, where shared USB drives or scanners need USB 3.0 speed.
caveats: Owners report a 1 to 2 second USB re-enumeration pause after each switch.
TESmart's guidance: at 4K 60 Hz, keep the monitor cable under 5 m (16 ft). Power on the monitor first, then the KVM, then connect the PCs.
Network control is set up with TESmart's Windows utility. The switch has no DHCP.
One monitor only. Use a dual-monitor model if each PC drives two screens.

products.name: TESmart HKS801-L23 8-Port HDMI KVM Switch, 4K 30 Hz, RS232/LAN Control
specs: 4K at 30 Hz per TESmart's title (the description says 60 Hz; plan on 30 Hz at 4K)
Front buttons, keyboard hotkeys, IR remote, RS232 and TCP/IP commands
PiKVM's built-in tesmart driver switches TESmart LAN models over the network
products.warranty: 1-year limited warranty in the US. Registering the KVM with TESmart extends it (TESmart's support pages say 2 to 3 years).
products.returns: 30-day returns on tesmart.com; free US shipping.
products.summary: The low-cost way to put 8 machines behind one keyboard, mouse and HDMI monitor, with serial and network control that PiKVM can drive.
products.fit: A homelab rack of servers or mini PCs used at 1080p or 1440p, especially with a PiKVM in front for remote access.
caveats: TESmart's title rates it at 4K 30 Hz. Buy the HKS801-P23 if you need 4K 60 Hz.
Behind a PiKVM, 3 of 3 owners in one Techno Tim thread hit EDID or black-screen problems. They fixed them with an EDID adapter, an HDMI splitter, or by removing the 4K emulators.
The default IP is 192.168.1.10 with no DHCP. You change it with TESmart's Windows utility, and the change takes effect only after a power cycle (PiKVM docs).
USB 2.0 only. Fine for keyboards and mice, slow for drives.
The price is a sale price; TESmart's list price is higher.

products.name: TESmart HKS801-M24 8-Port HDMI 2.1 KVM Switch, 4K 144 Hz / 8K 60 Hz, USB 3.2 Gen 1
specs: HDMI 2.1, 48 Gb/s, up to 8K at 60 Hz 4:4:4, 4K at 120/144 Hz
VRR (G-Sync, FreeSync), ALLM, FVA, HDR10 and Dolby Vision
Front buttons, hotkeys (Scroll Lock or Right Ctrl), mouse-wheel double-click, IR remote
products.warranty: 1-year limited warranty in the US. Registering the KVM with TESmart extends it (TESmart's support pages say 2 to 3 years).
products.returns: 30-day returns on tesmart.com; free US shipping.
products.summary: The 8-port KVM for high-refresh screens: HDMI 2.1 with 4K at 144 Hz and VRR passed through from up to 8 PCs.
products.fit: Several gaming or editing PCs that share one 4K 120 to 144 Hz monitor.
caveats: TESmart's product text mentions a LAN port for TCP/IP control, but its spec table lists only four switching methods for the 8-port model. Ask TESmart before you rely on network control.
You only get 144 Hz if the GPU, cables and monitor all support HDMI 2.1.

codes.terms: Shown as a copy-to-clipboard code on the tesmart.com home page on 2026-11-10; the site does not state the discount, end date or eligible products.

notes: Query choice: '8 port kvm switch'. The pages ranking for it now are store listings (StarTech, Dell, Adorama), reseller pages and dated SEO roundups, with no hands-on comparison. TESmart has the widest 8-port HDMI line, and PiKVM ships a built-in driver for TESmart LAN models. Pain points with counts: black screen or lost video after switching (5: 3 owners in the Techno Tim discussion, 1 MT-VIKI owner on the GL.iNet forum, 1 Trustpilot buyer); USB ports dying while video still works (6 users in one TESmart community thread, models HKS401-P23, HDC202-P23, HDC403-P23, HKS1601A1U and a 2-port kit, none of them the 8-port); network or RS232 setup clumsy (3: PiKVM docs, review-rating.com summary, Techno Tim); 4K 30 vs 60 Hz spec confusion (3 listings); USB re-enumeration pause of 1 to 2 s (2); hotkeys only from the dedicated port (2); short 1.5 m cables (2); weak IR remote (2). Segment winners: desk 4K60 with USB 3 goes to TESmart HKS801-P23; budget homelab or PiKVM front end goes to TESmart HKS801-L23; remote-first with per-server ATX power goes to the PiKVM Switch (not ours, named honestly); 4K144 gaming goes to TESmart HKS801-M24; cheapest local option without network control is MT-VIKI (Amazon-only, no price shown per the temporary rule). Verified 2026-11-10 with storecheck search on tesmart.com: P23 $399.00 in stock; L23 $143.99 (compare-at $239.99) in stock; M24 $599.00 in stock; EB23 $229.00 in stock. storecheck 'product' and WebFetch of the product pages returned HTTP 429 all session, so variant lists and the full spec tables were not read. The prices come from the store's own search feed, not snippets. Unverified and kept off the page: whether the P23 has a physical LAN port (the title says RS232/LAN, the description lists only RS232); M24 LAN control (the listing text and spec table conflict, so it is a caveat); exact count of shared USB 3.0 ports on the P23; StarTech R8AH202 price (about $700 per reseller snippets only) and its USB and EDID details; MT-VIKI specs (from reseller listings and manual snippets) and whether mt-viki.com is its official site (the footer company name matches, the domain was not confirmed); TESmart extended-warranty length (support pages say 2 and 3 years, the home banner says up to 5). The BLACKFRIDAY code appears on the TESmart home page with no stated terms. It has not been tested.
